# Mould Technical Specification & Complete Reference (llms-full.txt)

> Full system reference and documentation for LLMs and AI Agents interacting with `moul`.

---

## 1. System Overview & Technical Stack

`moul` is a self-contained dynamic database, multi-factor authentication, background worker processing, feature flag, and observability engine written in Go.

### Core Dependencies
- **HTTP Engine**: Echo v5 (`github.com/labstack/echo/v5`)
- **Web Admin Console**: TanStack Router (file-based routing), Meta StyleX (`@stylexjs/stylex` with `@stylexjs/unplugin`), Moul UI (`@moul-dev/ui`) with tri-state system/light/dark theming, TanStack Table & Query, Phosphor Icons (`@phosphor-icons/react`), and unified TanStack DevTools suite (`@tanstack/react-devtools`, `@tanstack/devtools-vite`, `@tanstack/devtools-event-client`) with typed runtime inspection, embedded via Go `//go:embed all:dist`.
- **Database Abstraction**: `github.com/pocketbase/dbx`
- **SQLite Engine**: `modernc.org/sqlite` (Pure Go, CGO-free)
- **TUI Framework**: Charm Bubble Tea (`charm.land/bubbletea/v2`)
- **MCP Protocol**: `github.com/mark3labs/mcp-go`
- **Rules Engine**: `github.com/expr-lang/expr`
- **S3 Replication**: `github.com/benbjohnson/litestream`

---

## 2. Environment Variables & Configuration

The engine reads environment variables from `.env` in the current working directory.

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `MOUL_ENV` | `development` | Environment mode (`development` or `production`). |
| `MOUL_PORT` | `8090` | HTTP server listening port. |
| `MOUL_PUBLIC_URL` | `http://localhost:8090` | Base public URL for email links. |
| `MOUL_JWT_SECRET` | Required | Secret key used for signing JWT tokens. |
| `MOUL_ADMIN_KEY` | Required | Admin key for elevated API endpoints and TUI access. |
| `MOUL_DB_PATH` | `moul-local.db` | Path to SQLite database file. |
| `MOUL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` | `""` | Master encryption key (min 16 bytes) for `cloak` AES-256-GCM encryption and blind indexes. |
| `MOUL_CORS_ORIGINS` | `*` (in dev) | Comma-separated list of allowed CORS origins. |
| `GEOIP_DB_PATH` | `""` | Optional path to MaxMind GeoIP2 `.mmdb` database. |
| `MOUL_TRUSTED_PROXIES` | `loopback` | Reverse proxies allowed to forward the client IP (IPs, CIDRs, `loopback`, `private`, `none`). |
| `MOUL_CLIENT_IP_HEADER` | `""` | Single-value client IP header set by the trusted edge proxy (e.g. `CF-Connecting-IP`). |
| `MOUL_FILE_URL_TTL` | `1h` | Minimum validity of signed file URLs (`?sig=`). |
| `MOUL_TOKEN_TTL` | `24h` | Lifetime of auth tokens. |
| `MOUL_ROOT_TOKEN_TTL` | `MOUL_TOKEN_TTL` | Lifetime of root user tokens. |
| `MOUL_TOKEN_REFRESH_GRACE` | `168h` | How long after expiry a token may still be refreshed (once); `0s` disables. |

---

## 3. Database Architecture & Meta-Tables

`moul` stores metadata and system states in reserved system tables prefixed with an underscore (`_`), which are automatically and idempotently created on first startup:

1. **`_moul`**: Stores schema metadata for all dynamic collections.
   - Columns: `id` (TEXT PRIMARY KEY), `name` (TEXT UNIQUE), `type` (TEXT), `fields` (TEXT JSON), `rules` (TEXT JSON), `email_templates` (TEXT JSON), `webhooks` (TEXT JSON), `createdAt` (TEXT), `updatedAt` (TEXT).
2. **`_visits`**: Stores deduplicated visitor session analytics.
3. **`_requests`**: Log table storing HTTP request logs asynchronously.
4. **`_settings`**: Key-value store for app settings (e.g. SMTP, Litestream, S3, rate limiting config).
5. **`_rootUsers`**: Master root administrator user credentials and accounts (columns: `id`, `username`, `email`, `name`, `passwordHash`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`).
6. **`_feature_flags`**: Feature flag definitions, rollouts, and gate configs.
7. **`_certmagic`**: TLS certificate and lock storage for automatic HTTPS management.
8. **`_revoked_tokens`**: Blacklist table for invalidated and revoked JWT authentication tokens.
9. **`_workers`**: Default system background worker job queue for built-in background tasks (SendEmail, cleanup routines) and zero-setup custom worker tasks.
10. **`_files`**: Uploaded files and who uploaded them (`id`, `ownerMoul`, `ownerId`, `createdAt`).
11. **`_file_refs`**: Which record fields reference each upload (`fileId`, `moul`, `recordId`, `field`); drives `/storage` access control.

---

## 4. Collection Schema Specification & Field Types

Collections can be of four primary types:
- `base`: Standard custom table for user-defined records.
- `auth`: Authentication collection (includes password, OTP, passkeys, OAuth2 social login, JWT handling).
- `worker`: Background worker job queue table (stores Oban-style job states).
- `analytic`: Event tracking collection.

### Supported Field Types
- `text`: String data.
- `number`: Numeric float or integer.
- `bool`: Boolean flag (0 or 1 in SQLite).
- `date`: Date string (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
- `datetime`: Date and time timestamp string (ISO 8601).
- `json`: Structured JSON payload stored as text.
- `url`: Web address link string (HTTP/HTTPS).
- `file`: File upload metadata reference.
- `select`: Constrained option string matching `options: ["A", "B"]`.
- `relation`: Relational reference to another collection with `relationConfig: {"targetMoul":"...", "cardinality":"1:1|1:N|M:N", "onDelete":"CASCADE|SET_NULL|RESTRICT"}`.
  - `1:1` and `1:N` store a single foreign key string ID in a `TEXT` column.
  - `M:N` uses a **Document / JSON Array model**, storing a JSON array of target record string IDs (e.g. `["id1", "id2"]`) inside a single `TEXT` column. No physical SQL junction table is created; relational queries operate via SQLite `json_each()` subqueries.
- `cloak`: Authenticated encrypted binary stored as SQLite `BLOB` using AES-256-GCM (`[0x01][nonce][ciphertext+tag]`) with HKDF-SHA256 derived keys.
  - Setting `searchable: true` automatically creates an indexed companion column `<fieldName>Hash TEXT` with HMAC-SHA256 blind indexes for exact equality filtering (`=` and `!=`). Range and pattern operators return 400 Bad Request.
  - Responses mask values by default (`••••` + last 4 chars). Admins always receive unmasked decrypted values; clients can unmask via `?reveal=field1,field2` (or `?reveal=all`). Companion hash columns are stripped from all API outputs. Requires `MOUL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`.

### Field Naming Constraints & Universal Timestamps
- **Strict camelCase**: All custom field names must match regex `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$` (e.g. `authorId`, `viewsCount`, `isFeatured`). Snake_case, PascalCase, dashes, and reserved words are rejected with HTTP 400.
- **Universal Timestamps**: Every collection table automatically creates and maintains `createdAt` and `updatedAt` ISO 8601 UTC timestamp columns. Reserved field names (`id`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `createdat`, `updatedat`) cannot be used for custom fields.

---

## 5. Authorization Rules Syntax

Collections enforce access rules for `List`, `View`, `Create`, `Update`, and `Delete` operations using expression engine syntax.

### Environment Macros & Placeholders
- `@request.auth.id`: Authenticated user's ID.
- `@request.auth.email`: Authenticated user's email.
- `@request.auth.username`: Authenticated user's username.
- `@collection.<table_name>.<field_name>`: Evaluates relationship or lookup table fields.
- `@now`: Current UTC timestamp string.

### Example Rules
- Allow public read: `""` (empty string)
- Require authentication: `@request.auth.id != ""`
- Owner restriction: `id = @request.auth.id` or `userId = @request.auth.id`
- RBAC role check (`users` auth collection):
  - Prevent role tampering during signup: `@request.body.role:isset = false || @request.body.role = 'public' || (@collection.users.id = @request.auth.id && @collection.users.role = 'admin')`
  - Prevent self-promotion on update: `(@collection.users.id = @request.auth.id && @collection.users.role = 'admin') || (id = @request.auth.id && @request.body.role:changed = false)`
- Downstream collection role enforcement (e.g. `posts`):
  - Public read, editor write own, admin full:
    - `list`: `status = 'published' || (@collection.users.id = @request.auth.id && (@collection.users.role = 'editor' || @collection.users.role = 'admin'))`
    - `create`: `@collection.users.id = @request.auth.id && (@collection.users.role = 'editor' || @collection.users.role = 'admin')`
    - `update`: `(@collection.users.id = @request.auth.id && @collection.users.role = 'admin') || (authorId = @request.auth.id && @collection.users.id = @request.auth.id && @collection.users.role = 'editor')`
    - `delete`: `@collection.users.id = @request.auth.id && @collection.users.role = 'admin'`

### Auth Collection Default Access Rules
When creating an `auth` collection, default access rules are automatically configured across the Web Admin Console, `moul-ctl`, and backend engine:
- `list`: `id = @request.auth.id` (restricts querying/listing to the authenticated user)
- `view`: `id = @request.auth.id` (users can only view their own record)
- `create`: `""` (empty string; allows open user registration / sign-up via `POST /api/moul/{name}/records`)
- `update`: `id = @request.auth.id` (users can only edit their own profile)
- `delete`: `id = @request.auth.id` (users can only delete their own account)

---

## 6. Complete REST API Route Reference

### Web Admin Console & Docs
- `GET /_moul_/`: Embedded Web Admin Console (TanStack Router + StyleX SPA).
- `GET /_moul_/*`: Static asset serving (`/assets/*`) with immutable cache header, and HTML5 SPA fallback to `index.html`.
- `GET /admin` / `GET /_moul_`: Automatic 301 redirects to `/_moul_/`.
- `GET /docs`: Interactive API Documentation UI (Scalar / Swagger).
- `GET /openapi.json`: Dynamic OpenAPI 3.0 Spec (JSON).
- `GET /openapi.yml`: Dynamic OpenAPI 3.0 Spec (YAML).
- `GET /AGENTS.md`: Agent documentation guide.
- `GET /llms.txt`: Standard LLM text reference index.
- `GET /llms-full.txt`: Complete LLM technical specification.

### Setup & Root User Management (Admin Auth)
- `GET /api/setup`: Check if initial setup is required (`needsSetup: true|false`).
- `POST /api/setup`: Register initial root user (`username`, `name`, `email`, `password`).
- `POST /api/admin/login`: Authenticate root user with Master Admin Key & credentials.
- `GET /api/admin/account` / `GET /api/settings/account`: Retrieve root user profile (`username`, `name`, `email`, etc.).
- `PATCH /api/admin/account` / `PATCH /api/settings/account`: Update root user account (`username`, `name`, `email`, and optional `password`).
- `POST /api/admin/password`: Update root user password (`currentPassword`, `password`, `passwordConfirm`, optional `identity`).
- `POST /api/admin/reload` / `POST /api/settings/reload`: Hot-reload runtime middleware (rate limiter, root IP allowlist), mailer, and TLS configurations.

### Built-in MCP Server & OAuth2 Discovery (Admin Auth & OAuth2)
- `ALL /api/mcp*`: Model Context Protocol Streamable HTTP & SSE server endpoint. Supports Bearer token auth (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`), dedicated header (`X-Admin-Key`), or OAuth 2.0 / 2.1 access tokens.
- `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` & `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/*`: RFC 9728 OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata for automatic discovery by AI clients (e.g. Google Gemini Custom Connected Apps). Returns authorization servers and supported scopes (`moul:mcp:admin`).
- `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` & `/.well-known/openid-configuration`: RFC 8414 OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata describing authorization, token, and registration endpoints with PKCE (`S256`).
- `POST /api/oauth2/register`: RFC 7591 Dynamic Client Registration endpoint allowing Gemini or other clients to register dynamically.
- `GET /api/oauth2/authorize` & `POST /api/oauth2/authorize`: OAuth 2.1 authorization consent endpoint supporting PKCE (`code_challenge`), login with root admin credentials or Admin Secret Key, and authorization code issuance.
- `POST /api/oauth2/token`: OAuth 2.1 token issuance exchanging authorization code or refresh token for a JWT Bearer access token.

### Collection Management (Admin Auth)
- `GET /api/moul`: List all collection schemas (root user token or admin key).
- `POST /api/moul`: Create new collection schema (`X-Admin-Key` or Admin Token).
- `PATCH /api/moul/:name`: Update collection schema.
- `DELETE /api/moul/:name`: Delete collection schema and drop physical SQLite table.

### Dynamic Record CRUD
> Note: Reserved system tables prefixed with `_*` (`_workers`, `_moul`, `_settings`, `_rootUsers`, etc.) are strictly protected and return `404 Not Found` on all `/api/moul/:name/records` endpoints. Use dedicated system routes instead.
- `GET /api/moul/:name/records`: List paginated records (`page`, `perPage`, `sort`, `filter`, `search`). Admin requests (`X-Admin-Key` or root user JWT) bypass listRule restrictions.
- `GET /api/moul/:name/records/:id`: Get single record by ID. Hidden records answer `404` like missing ones.
- `POST /api/moul/:name/records`: Create record.
- `PATCH /api/moul/:name/records/:id`: Update record by ID.
- `DELETE /api/moul/:name/records/:id`: Delete record by ID.
- `POST /api/realtime/ticket`: Exchange Bearer token or X-Admin-Key for a 30s single-use ticket (`ticket`, `expiresAt`, `expiresIn`). Supports optional `reveal` for admins (non-admins passing reveal receive HTTP 400).
- `GET /api/moul/:name/subscribe`: Real-time record subscription stream (SSE) for collection updates (`event`, `id`, `ticket` query params, or `Authorization: Bearer` header). Governed by continuous mid-stream authorization re-evaluation against `subscribeRule` / `viewRule` with transition-aware synthetic delete events. Cloak fields are masked (`••••1234`) and companion `<fieldName>Hash` stripped; `?reveal` requires root/admin credentials (non-admins receive HTTP 400). Query credentials (`?token=`, `?admin_key=`) are rejected with HTTP 400. Immediate disconnect (`event: auth_expired`) upon token expiry or revocation. Protected against DoS: bounded 128-event ring buffer per client with slow-consumer eviction (`event: slow_consumer`), 5s write deadlines on flushes, and per-user (15) / per-IP (30) concurrent stream quotas (HTTP 429).
- `GET /api/moul/subscribe`: Global real-time record subscription stream (SSE) across collections (`?mouls=posts,comments&ticket=...`) with continuous per-event authorization re-evaluation, cloak field masking, hash stripping, slow-consumer eviction, 5s write deadlines, and concurrent connection quotas.
- `GET /api/moul/:name/export`: Export records in CSV or JSON format (`?format=csv|json&schema=true`). Admin requests only (`X-Admin-Key` or root user JWT).
- `POST /api/moul/:name/import`: Import records from CSV or JSON payload (`?mode=upsert|insert|replace&error_strategy=atomic|continue`). Supports multipart/form-data (`file` field) or direct payload (`Content-Type: text/csv` or `application/json`). Admin requests only.

### Authentication Endpoints (For `auth` type collections)
- `POST /api/moul/:name/auth-with-password`: Login with username/email & password.
- `POST /api/moul/:name/otp/request`: Request email OTP code.
- `POST /api/moul/:name/auth-with-otp`: Verify OTP code (5 guesses per code, 20 failures per account per day, 30 per client network per 10 minutes; `429` with `Retry-After` beyond).
- `POST /api/moul/:name/passkey/login/options`: Get WebAuthn assertion options.
- `POST /api/moul/:name/passkey/login/verify`: Verify WebAuthn assertion.
- `GET /api/moul/:name/auth-methods`: List active authentication methods & configured OAuth2 providers.
- `GET /api/moul/:name/oauth2/:provider`: Initiate OAuth2 login/signup (github, google, apple).
- `GET /api/moul/:name/oauth2/:provider/callback`: Handle OAuth2 provider code callback.
- `POST /api/moul/:name/auth-with-oauth2`: Authenticate with OAuth2 code (for SPAs and mobile apps).
- `POST /api/oauth2/device/authorize`: Init OAuth2 device flow code.
- `POST /api/oauth2/device/token`: Poll for OAuth2 device access token.

### Background Worker Management (`/api/workers` - root user token or admin key)
- `GET /api/workers`: List background jobs from the built-in `_workers` queue with pagination (`page`, `perPage`), status filter (`state`), queue filter (`queue`), worker filter (`worker`), and sorting (`sort`).
- `POST /api/workers`: Enqueue a background job directly into the `_workers` system table (`worker`, `queue`, `args`, `meta`, `tags`, `priority`, `max_attempts`, `scheduled_at`).
- `GET /api/workers/:id`: Get details of a single background job by ID.
- `PATCH /api/workers/:id`: Update job state (e.g. `available`, `discarded`, `cancelled`) or rescheduled time. Setting to `available` resets attempt counter and triggers execution.
- `DELETE /api/workers/:id`: Permanently delete a job record from `_workers`.
- `POST /api/workers/retry`: Reset discarded, cancelled, or specific worker jobs in `_workers` back to `available` state for immediate processing.

### Request Observability & Analytics (root user token or admin key)
- `GET /api/requests`: List tracked HTTP request logs with pagination (`page`, `perPage`).
- `GET /api/requests/:id`: Get tracked HTTP request details.
- `GET /api/visits`: List visit sessions with pagination.
- `GET /api/visits/:id`: Get visit session details.

### Feature Flags
> Flag management requires a root user token or the admin key; any signed-in user may evaluate (identity attributes are pinned to the caller).
- `GET /api/feature-flags`: List feature flags.
- `POST /api/feature-flags`: Create feature flag.
- `GET /api/feature-flags/:key`: Get flag by key.
- `PATCH /api/feature-flags/:key`: Update flag parameters/gates.
- `DELETE /api/feature-flags/:key`: Delete flag.
- `POST /api/feature-flags/:key/eval`: Evaluate flag for a given context.

---

## 6a. Security Defaults

Moul ships secure by default. The behaviors below apply to every caller that is neither a root user (`_rootUsers` token) nor the admin key.

- **Admin surface**: schemas (`/api/moul`, `/api/moul/:name`, webhooks, email templates, export/import), settings, file listing and deletion, workers, retry-jobs, visits, requests, feature flag management, system metrics, the rules sandbox and MCP accept only a root user token or the admin key, and only they get collection schemas in `/openapi.json` / `/openapi.yml` (others get the static engine spec). Guests get `401` (with the OAuth discovery challenge), members of other auth collections `403`. Members keep `POST /api/upload` and `POST /api/feature-flags/:key/eval` (identity attributes and a percentage rollout's attribute are pinned to the caller and `org_id` is dropped; other attributes such as `groups` and `role` remain client-asserted, so flags are not an authorization mechanism).
- **Client IP**: forwarding headers are honored only from trusted proxies. By default only loopback is trusted (a reverse proxy or tunnel agent on the same host). A proxy in another container or on the LAN needs `MOUL_TRUSTED_PROXIES` (IPs, CIDRs, `loopback`, `private` for every private network, or `none`); use `private` only when no client can reach Moul from a private address (NAT setups such as Docker Desktop or Kubernetes SNAT). Optionally set `MOUL_CLIENT_IP_HEADER` (e.g. `CF-Connecting-IP`). Rate limits, the root IP allowlist, OTP throttling, the request log and visits all use this address.
- **Hidden records answer like missing ones**: `GET`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` on `/api/moul/:name/records/:id` check the `viewRule` first; a record the caller may not view answers `404 Record not found`, byte for byte the answer for an unknown id (`401` for both when the presented bearer token was rejected, so clients still notice an expired session). Relation targets of a create are validated only after the `createRule` passes.
- **Filters, sorts and search**: the `listRule` and `?filter=` bind their values under separate placeholders, so a filter can never rewrite the rule. Client filters may not use `@collection`, and neither filters nor sorts may reference secret columns (`passwordHash`, `tokenKey`, OTP and reset columns, `oauthProviders`, and the `email` of auth collections). Relation paths (`author.name = 'x'`) only match target records the caller may list; sorting through a relation requires a publicly listable target. Every column, including relation targets, is validated against the schema before it reaches SQL. `?search=` skips emails, and the `?after=` cursor is read under the caller's `listRule`.
- **Responses**: secrets (`passwordHash`, `tokenKey`, OTP, `resetToken`, `resetTokenExpiresAt`, `oauthProviders`, cloak blind indexes) never leave the server. The `email` of an auth record reaches only admins and the user themself, unless the collection has a bool field `emailVisibility` and the record sets it. `?expand=` applies the target collection's `viewRule`: hidden to-one targets are `null`, hidden to-many targets are omitted. Realtime events are redacted per subscriber.
- **Ownership**: a column the `updateRule` pins to the caller (`owner = @request.auth.id`) cannot be changed to anyone else on update (`403`); resending the stored value is fine. Number fields store canonical numbers; strings must be plain decimals of at most 32 bytes.
- **Files**: Moul records who uploaded each file and which record fields reference it. `/storage/<id>/<name>` is served without a signature only when a guest could view a record that references the file; otherwise it needs a `?sig=` signature (returned in record responses, expands, realtime events and the upload response, valid at least `MOUL_FILE_URL_TTL`, default `1h`), the uploader, or a caller who may view a referencing record. Anything else answers the same `404` as a missing file. With S3 enabled, `/storage` presigns a short redirect, so the bucket can be private. File field values must point to their own upload under `/storage`, and members may attach only files they uploaded (or files the record already holds).
- **Uploads**: members may not upload HTML, SVG, XML, scripts or CSS (by extension, declared or sniffed type); the `file_allowed_types` setting (e.g. `image/*,application/pdf`) narrows uploads further. Stored files are served with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, a sandboxing Content-Security-Policy, a type taken from the extension, and as an attachment unless they are images, audio or video.
- **OTP sign-in**: each issued code allows 5 guesses (then it is voided), each account 20 failures per day, and each client network (IPv4 address or IPv6 /64) 30 failures per 10 minutes; exceeding one answers `429` with `Retry-After`. Codes are compared in constant time and never logged when a mailer or worker can deliver them.

---

## 7. Built-in MCP Server Tool Specifications

The built-in MCP server provides 17 tools accessible over stdio (`moul mcp` or `<custom-binary> mcp`) or Streamable HTTP & SSE (`/api/mcp`):

1. `moul_list_collections`: List all dynamic collection schemas and tables.
2. `moul_get_collection`: `{"name": "string"}` - Retrieve schema details.
3. `moul_create_collection`: `{"name": "string", "type": "base|auth|worker|analytic", "fields_json": "string"}` (fields: `text`, `number`, `bool`, `date`, `datetime`, `json`, `url`, `file`, `select`, `relation`).
4. `moul_delete_collection`: `{"name": "string"}`.
5. `moul_list_records`: `{"collection": "string", "page": int, "per_page": int}`.
6. `moul_get_record`: `{"collection": "string", "id": "string"}`.
7. `moul_create_record`: `{"collection": "string", "data_json": "string"}`.
8. `moul_update_record`: `{"collection": "string", "id": "string", "data_json": "string"}`.
9. `moul_delete_record`: `{"collection": "string", "id": "string"}`.
10. `moul_list_worker_jobs`: `{"table": "string", "state": "string", "limit": int}`.
11. `moul_enqueue_job`: `{"table": "string", "worker": "string", "args_json": "string", "queue": "string", "priority": int}`.
12. `moul_cancel_job`: `{"table": "string", "id": "string"}`.
13. `moul_list_feature_flags`: List feature flags and targeting rules.
14. `moul_set_feature_flag`: `{"key": "string", "enabled": bool, "description": "string", "default_value": "string"}`.
15. `moul_get_system_metrics`: Retrieve host system CPU, RAM, Disk, Load telemetry snapshot.
16. `moul_get_analytics_summary`: Retrieve visitor and request totals.
17. `moul_list_requests`: `{"limit": int}` - Query recent HTTP request logs.

### MCP Client Configuration (`.cursor/mcp.json` / `mcpServers`)

#### Option 1: Bearer Token Authentication (Recommended)
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "moul": {
      "type": "http",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ADMIN_SECRET_KEY"
      },
      "url": "http://localhost:8090/api/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

#### Option 2: Dedicated Admin Key Header (`X-Admin-Key`)
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "moul": {
      "type": "http",
      "headers": {
        "X-Admin-Key": "ADMIN_SECRET_KEY"
      },
      "url": "http://localhost:8090/api/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

#### Option 3: Google Gemini Custom Connected Apps (OAuth 2.0 / 2.1)
- MCP Server URL: `https://<your-host>/api/mcp`
- Discovery: RFC 9728 (`/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`) and RFC 8414 (`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`).
- Dynamic Client Registration: Fully supports RFC 7591 automatic client registration.
- Consent & Authorization: Users approve access on the interactive consent screen using Root Administrator credentials (email/username and password), fully decoupled from the Admin Key.

---

## 8. Programmatic Go Extensibility & HTTP Route Hooks (`pkg/app`)

`moul` provides a public Go package `github.com/moul-dev/moul-dev/pkg/app` to embed the engine into custom applications and attach custom HTTP routes, background workers, or custom MCP tools without forking code.

### Core API Methods & Hooks
- `app.OnRecordBeforeCreate/Update/Delete(fn, collections...)` and `app.OnRecordAfterCreate/Update/Delete(fn, collections...)`: Go record hooks that run for HTTP and programmatic writes alike (`*app.RecordEvent`: `Action`, `Collection`, `Record`, `OldRecord`, `Auth`, `Admin`, `Context`). A before hook's error refuses the change (`*echo.HTTPError` picks the status, 400 otherwise).
- `app.Records()`: Go record API with admin rights (`Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, `Get`, `List`) running the full HTTP pipeline (validation, rules, webhooks, realtime events, file tracking, hooks); `.AsUser(collection, id)` applies collection rules as that user; `.Notify(ctx, app.RecordCreate|RecordUpdate|RecordDelete, collection, id, old)` announces raw SQL writes to hooks, webhooks and realtime subscribers.
- `app.WithTokenTTL(d)`, `app.WithCollectionTokenTTL(collection, d)`, `app.WithTokenRefreshGrace(d)`: auth token lifetime (default 24h) and refresh grace (default 7 days).
- `app.Config`: Holds engine configuration including `APIPrefix *string` (default `nil` resolves to `"/api"`, set to `&""` to mount at root), `AdminUIFS fs.FS`, `AdminUIPrefix string` (default `/_moul_`), and `DisableAdminUI bool`.
- `app.WithAPIPrefix(prefix string) *app.App`: Sets the URL path prefix for API endpoints (e.g. `"/v1"` or `""` for root).
- `app.WithAdminUI(fs fs.FS) *app.App`: Overrides the default embedded Web Admin Console with a custom frontend SPA distribution.
- `app.WithAdminPrefix(prefix string) *app.App`: Sets the URL mount prefix for the Web Admin Console.
- `app.DisableAdminUI() *app.App`: Disables mounting the Web Admin Console routes entirely for headless microservices.
- `app.WithAdminRedirect(enable bool) *app.App`: Deprecated and no-op; `/admin` redirects are removed to avoid collisions with root routes.
- `app.DefaultAdminFS() fs.FS`: Accesses the default embedded Web Admin Console filesystem from `pkg/ui`.
- `app.RegisterRoute(method, path string, handler echo.HandlerFunc, middleware ...echo.MiddlewareFunc)`: Expressive shorthand method to register routes directly on the embedded Echo server.
- `app.OnRouterInit(fn func(router *echo.Echo) error)`: Hook invoked during `Bootstrap()` right after the Echo router is constructed. Allows creating router groups, custom Echo middlewares, and specialized handlers.
- `app.OnBeforeStart(fn func(app *app.App) error)`: Hook invoked at the end of `Bootstrap()` before listeners start. Gives full access to `app.DB()`, `app.Router()`, `app.WorkerEngine()`, `app.Mailer()`, `app.AnalyticsEngine()`, and `app.MCPServer()`.
- `app.RegisterWorker(name string, handler worker.JobHandler)`: Registers a custom background job worker (from `pkg/worker` or `app.JobHandler`).
- `app.RegisterPeriodicWorker(interval time.Duration, name string, handler worker.JobHandler)`: Registers a periodic background task.
- `app.OnWorkerInit(fn func(engine *worker.Engine) error)`: Hook executed when worker engine initializes (`pkg/worker.Engine`).
- `app.RegisterMCPTool(tool mcp.Tool, handler server.ToolHandlerFunc)`: Registers a custom MCP tool exposed over both stdio and HTTP transports.
- `app.OnMCPInit(fn func(srv *moulmcp.Server) error)`: Hook executed when the MCP server is initialized.
- `app.MCPServer() *moulmcp.Server`: Accesses the built-in MCP server instance to inspect or attach custom MCP tools.
- `app.ServeMCP(ctx context.Context) error`: Starts the built-in MCP server over stdio (auto-dispatched on `mcp` command without requiring HTTP secrets).
- `app.IsMCP() bool`: Utility reporting whether the binary was invoked in MCP mode.


### Code Example
```go
package main

import (
	"context"
	"net/http"

	"github.com/labstack/echo/v5"
	"github.com/moul-dev/moul-dev/pkg/app"
	"github.com/moul-dev/moul-dev/pkg/worker"
)

func main() {
	// The Web Admin Console is automatically bundled and served at "/_moul_/"
	moulApp := app.New(app.Config{
		Version: "1.0.0-custom",
	})

	// Optional: customize API prefix, mount prefix, supply custom SPA filesystem, or disable
	// moulApp.WithAPIPrefix("/v1") // customize API prefix (use "" for root)
	// moulApp.WithAdminPrefix("/dashboard")
	// moulApp.WithAdminUI(myCustomFS)
	// moulApp.DisableAdminUI()

	// Register custom HTTP route
	moulApp.RegisterRoute("GET", "/api/custom/ping", func(c *echo.Context) error {
		return c.JSON(http.StatusOK, map[string]string{"status": "pong"})
	})

	// Access raw Echo router via hook
	moulApp.OnRouterInit(func(router *echo.Echo) error {
		router.GET("/api/custom/health", func(c *echo.Context) error {
			return c.String(http.StatusOK, "OK")
		})
		return nil
	})

	// Register custom background worker
	moulApp.RegisterWorker("CustomTask", func(ctx context.Context, job *worker.Job) error {
		return nil
	})

	moulApp.Start(context.Background())
}
```

---

## 9. Essential CLI Commands

```bash
# Start HTTP engine server (default port 8090)
moul start

# Seed database with realistic collections, demo records, and feature flags
moul seed

# Export collection records to CSV or JSON
moul export posts --format=csv --out=posts.csv
moul export posts --format=json --out=posts.json --schema

# Import collection records from CSV or JSON
moul import posts posts.csv --mode=upsert
moul import posts posts.json --mode=replace --error-strategy=continue

# Generate TypeScript type definitions from collection schemas
moul typegen --out ui/src/types/schema.d.ts

# Test and validate a rule expression against mock record/auth context
moul test-rule --rule="authorId = @request.auth.id" --record='{"authorId": "usr_1"}' --auth='{"id": "usr_1"}'

# Manage worker jobs / retry dead-letter queue (DLQ)
moul worker retry tasks_queue [job_id]
moul worker list-failed tasks_queue

# Start built-in MCP server over stdio
moul mcp

# Launch Bubble Tea TUI Admin Console
moul-ctl -server http://localhost:8090 -admin-key test-admin-key-1234
# Or via convenience subcommand in moul:
moul ctl -server http://localhost:8090 -admin-key test-admin-key-1234
```

---

## 10. Production Deployment (LXD + Tailscale + Cloudflare Tunnel)

For hardened enterprise production environments on **Ubuntu Server 26.04 LTS**:
- **Host Containerization**: Run `moul` inside unprivileged LXD system containers (`lxc launch ubuntu:26.04 moul-prod`).
- **Host Administration**: Install Tailscale on the host FIRST. Restrict SSH access (port 22) exclusively to the `tailscale0` interface (`ufw allow in on tailscale0 to any port 22`) and close all public inbound host ports (`ufw default deny incoming`).
- **Zero-Trust Public Ingress**: Route public HTTPS traffic to the LXD container port 8090 using Cloudflare Tunnel (`cloudflared`).
- **Database Backups**: Configure Litestream S3 replication for point-in-time SQLite disaster recovery.
- Full Step-by-Step Guide: [docs/deployment-lxd-tailscale-cloudflare.md](/docs/deployment-lxd-tailscale-cloudflare.md)
